Subject: Montara private connector - egress allowlist & proxy questions

Hi Camila,

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. A few follow-ups from our security and network teams as we prepare the on-prem integration for the private connector:

- We need clarity on what exactly must be allowlisted on our firewall for the control plane and for the tenant proxy. Do you require IPs (static) or will FQDN/SNI be sufficient?
- For the control plane control traffic (account management, telemetry), can Redwood provide a stable set of source IPs (or a CIDR) we can block/allow?
- For inference traffic that egresses from our tenant proxy, does Redwood accept TLS (443) only to FQDNs, or do you need dedicated per-tenant IPs for auditing?
- Any required ports beyond 443? Do you inspect TLS SNI or require mTLS for the private deployment control plane?
- We also need a minimal acceptance checklist (what evidence you need from our side: NAT logs, jumpbox IPs, proxy headers) so we can prepare procurement and firewall change windows.

Attaching our initial network diagram (see inline) — we can share more if helpful. Can we schedule a 30-min follow-up next week with network/security?

Thanks,
Rajiv
Network Security Lead
Montara Health

Hi Rajiv — great questions. TL;DR: we support two common deployment patterns and can provide a short acceptance checklist. Details below; I included the minimal outbound list and a CSV with IPs/FQDNs attached (egress-ip-matrix.csv).

Deployment patterns (choose one):
1) Redwood-managed control plane egress (recommended for fastest onboarding)
   - Redwood will egress control-plane traffic from a small set of stable IPs (we can provide up to 6 static IPv4 addresses).
   - Customer allowlists those IPs for control plane API/telemetry endpoints.
   - Tenant inference traffic still originates from customer-managed proxy/NAT (see 2).

2) Fully customer-managed egress (common for stricter network controls / on-prem)
   - Customer NAT/proxy handles outbound to Redwood. We accept TLS to FQDNs; we prefer SNI-based allowlisting for flexibility.
   - If your compliance requires per-tenant source IPs, customers can map tenant proxies to stable egress IPs and provide that mapping to us for auditing.

Minimal outbound allowlist (control plane and required hosts):
- FQDNs: control.redwood-inference.com, model-catalog.redwood-inference.com, auth.redwood-inference.com, metrics.redwood-collector.net
- Ports: 443 outbound (primary). 123/UDP only if NTP is inspected (rare).
- TLS: SNI is sufficient for routing; mTLS is optional for customers who want mutual authentication (we can enable per-deployment).
- IPs: attached CSV contains the current set of control-plane egress IPs (subject to change with notice).

Evidence we typically request from customers for acceptance:
- NAT egress mapping (source IP -> tenant-id) or CIDR block used for outbound.
- Firewall rule snapshots showing the allowlist.
- A brief connectivity test (curl -v to control.redwood-inference.com) and an exported packet capture if TLS inspection rejects traffic.

Operational notes:
- We support SNI-based allowlisting but recommend an extra IP-based rule for control-plane to reduce risk from DNS interception during outage windows.
- If you plan TLS inspection (TLS interception / enterprise proxy), please coordinate a short test — interception can break cert pinning on some connections.

Next steps: I can run a 30-min tech call next Tue/Thu. If you agree to provide the NAT mapping and firewall snapshot, we’ll prepare the acceptance checklist and a temporary test token for connectivity checks.

Regards,
Camila Reyes
Account Lead, North America
Redwood Inference

Attachment: egress-ip-matrix.csv (CSV stub)

Quick internal note — adding a couple of clarifications before we lock the checklist:

- For customers on our private (VPC/on-prem) plan we can commit to providing stable control-plane source IPs but require a 90-day notice window for changes to that set. Call that out if you need a SLA-backed IP guarantee.
- We can enable optional client cert authentication for the control-plane endpoints; helps when customers run TLS interception.
- If Montara wants per-tenant auditing, they should supply a CSV mapping tenant_id -> egress_ip. We will ingest that into our audit pipeline and surface it in Redwood Console (token-level attribution).

I'll prepare a short acceptance checklist fragment for Camila to share that lists the exact evidence items and our test commands.

-Karthik
Staff Infra Engineer
Redwood Inference
